name: Personal Kanban Work-in-Progress (WIP) Limits
diagnostic: Multitasking-induced lead time inflation. Unconstrained active work saturates attention, maximizes context-switching penalties, and slows end-to-end task throughput according to Little's Law.

procedure.text: Build a three-column board: Backlog, In-Flight, Done.
Cap In-Flight at three items for one person.
Pull a new item in only when an existing one is completed or discarded.
If the cap is breached, stop and fix the bottleneck before adding more work.

trap: Raising the cap whenever an exciting new task arrives, which removes the friction that forces focus and finishing.
procedureFull:
1. Construct a minimal three-stage visual board: Backlog, In-Flight, and Done.
2. Establish a hard numerical cap on the In-Flight column: WIP Limit ≤ 3 items for a solo operator.
3. Implement a strict pull dynamic: no new item may enter In-Flight from Backlog until an existing item moves to Done or is explicitly discarded.
4. Treat any WIP violation as an operational fault requiring immediate desynchronization of lower-priority tasks.
setupFull:
* Backlog
  * TODO Design database migration scripts #priority/medium
  * TODO Refactor authentication interceptor #priority/low
* In-Flight (WIP: 2 / MAX: 3)
  * DOING Implement OAuth token revocation endpoint
  * DOING Fix race condition in webhooks consumer
* Done
  * DONE Audit API endpoint latencies
trapFull: Arbitrarily adjusting WIP limits upward whenever exciting new tasks emerge, neutralizing the systemic friction that forces focus and project completion.
